newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Latin ADRs ease in New York market.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Latin ADRs ease in New York market.

text.p: Shares in Latin American companies were largely off in New York on Tuesday, reflecting uncertainty about Mexican privatization plans and Argentine political tension, traders and analysts said.
They also said American Depositary Receipts were following the lead of the larger market, which skidded to session lows in the early afternoon.
"All eyes are on the U.S. (and) volumes are relatively weak in all of these stocks. It's really on the back of Wall Street profit-taking," said Simon Edwards, a trader for UBS Securities.
By mid-afternoon, 136 of the 441 ADRs had risen and 146 had declined, with the rest unchanged. Volume was 38.1 million shares.
Argentine ADRs were off following accusations by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo that two cabinet ministers had tried to cover up corruption inquiries.
Telefonica de Argentina was off 3/4 to 24-1/2 and Telecom Argentina fell one point to 39-1/2 amid the political uncertainty caused by the charges.
Mexican ADRs were burdened by the weak peso, worries about the strength of the economy and news the Mexican government was backing off from plans to sell state petrochemical plants.

"There's been a bit of a setback in Mexico on the privatization news" and traders "were looking for reasons to sell off anyway," said Walter Molaro, director of economic and financial research at SBC Warburg.
Telefonos de Mexico was off 1/8 to 31-3/8 on volume of 2.15 million shares. Grupo Televisa fell 3/8 to 26-1/2.
Among other stocks, Glaxo Wellcome Plc was off 3/8 to 31-1/8 on profit-taking. Hanson Plc rose 1/4 to 6-5/8 following favorable comments in a Financial Times newspaper column.
